lines.text: Analysis of "Potential Medal" in Non-Medal-Winning Nations
The Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial model is employed to quantify the latent medal
potential of nations that have not yet won Olympic medals. This model integrates dynamic
variables like the weighted number of participants (Athletesit) and the degree of alignment
between a nation's historical strengths and the current Olympic program (ProjectMatchit).
• High-Match Nations: 38% of non-medal-winning nations exhibit a high project match
> 0.2) in at least one sport, indicating significant potential for
Resource Efficiency: A 1% increase in resource allocation efficiency (proxied by per
capita training expenditure) boosts the probability of medal success by 2.3% (p < 0.01).
The radar chart (Figure 22) visualizes the sport-specific potential distribution of three
representative medal-less nations. Saint Lucia demonstrates 85% matching potential in
sprinting, consistent with its historic gold medal breakthrough at Paris 2024. The asym-
metric polar coordinates emphasize strategic priorities.
Nations should prioritize targeted investment in high-match, low-resource sports.
6.2 The Multiplier Effect of Elite Coaches
The Bayesian Entropy Model is utilized to quantify the impact of elite coaches on medal
performance. The core metric, Information Gain (IG), measures the reduction in uncertainty
regarding medal outcomes due to coaching interventions. A threshold of IG > 0.3 indicates
Coach Effect: In sports with IG > 0.3, the introduction of elite coaches increases medal
counts by 1.82.5 times, with particularly pronounced effects in technically complex sports
